entries.name: Bowser, Warlord of Darkland
entries.look: Bowser — The Dragon-King Who Keeps Getting Up Bowser is the creature who has defined the Mushroom Kingdom through opposition for longer than most of its current inhabitants have been alive. He is the villain of every story, the kidnapper in every legend, the fire-breathing turtle-dragon-king whose name is used to frighten children and whose actual presence frightens things considerably larger than children. entries.name: Goomba (Conscript Infantry)
entries.look: Goomba — The Ones Who Die First The Goomba is the most common, most expendable, and most tragically undervalued member of the Koopa Troop's military structure. They are small mushroom-like creatures with no arms, stubby legs, prominent eyebrows that convey a permanent expression of mild indignation, and a combat life expectancy measured in seconds against competent opponents. entries.name: Hammer Bro (Elite Infantry)
entries.look: Hammer Bro — The Elite Who Earned It Hammer Bros are the Koopa Troop's elite infantry—koopas who distinguished themselves through combat performance and were promoted to a specialized role that combines armored durability with ranged firepower through the ancient koopa art of throwing hammers at things until those things stop being problems. entries.name: Koopa Troopa (Standard Infantry)
entries.look: Koopa Troopa — The Backbone Nobody Thanks The Koopa Troopa is the standard infantry soldier of the Koopa Troop, the bipedal turtle-people who have served as Bowser's primary ground forces for as long as anyone can remember. They walk patrol routes. They man fortress positions. They stand between Mario and whatever objective Mario is stomping toward. And they die—in enormous numbers, with depressing regularity, respawning through mechanisms that nobody fully understands and that the koopas themselves describe only as "it's a turtle thing." entries.name: Magikoopa (Battle Mage)
entries.look: Magikoopa — The Troop's Magical Backbone Magikoopas are the Koopa Troop's spellcasters—koopas who discovered magical aptitude and were trained in the traditions that Kamek established centuries ago. They wear blue robes, round spectacles that may or may not be prescription, and pointed hats that serve no magical function but have become traditional enough that going without one is considered professionally inappropriate. entries.name: Bob-omb Sapper
entries.look: Era sheet: Highsun 1, 955 BF, Peach's Castle. Art and stats describe this figure on the night of the Day Of (events.json highsun_1_955_bf_the_day_of ), not the present day of the campaign (1040 BF). Scene kit — The Interloper at the Council. Bowser and his force burst in on a crucial palace meeting. This is a GM scene kit, not a filed event; nothing on this sheet changes the canon record of what happened that night. Iron casing, wind-up key, lit fuse, a tool belt with a detonator plunger. The sapper is why the council doors are no longer doors.
